open_points.subject: TrialExecution file output disclosure class used for agent masking
open_points.text: M07: "for a `file` port only its facts — digest, size and media type, no bytes and never a StoredValue"; A07 rule 4: "The same holds for a `personal_data` file: an agent gets its digest and class".
open_points.question: Where does the disclosure class of a trial-execution file output come from, so `surface` can return digest+class to agents?
options: Store disclosure class on each trial-execution file output record
Derive it from the trial case inputs (highest class) at read time
Treat trial-execution file outputs as never `personal_data` (would contradict A07)
open_points.default_guess: Derive class from the trial case inputs (highest class) when reading, because no class field exists on M07 file outputs.

open_points.subject: Ownership of execution-class computation for masking
open_points.text: State 3 says both: "The class used for masking is computed by `surface` itself under A07 rule 5" and "a value a rule computes ... comes from the owning module's capability, never from `surface` re-deriving it."
open_points.question: Is execution class for A07 masking an explicit exception that `surface` must compute, or must another module own and expose this computed value?
options: Make execution-class computation an explicit `surface` exception
Move computation to an owning module capability (`runs`/`functions`/`effects`) and have `surface` call it
open_points.default_guess: Treat execution-class computation as an explicit `surface` exception for masking only.

open_points.subject: `spool_run_bytes_max` enforcement and outcome mapping
open_points.text: A15 rule 3 requires: "a run whose spooled files together exceed `spool_run_bytes_max`, concludes the producing element ..."; State 3 splits concerns: `store` "Must not own ... any outcome of a node", while `runs` owns spool lifecycle and `effects` owns operation-element outcomes.
open_points.question: Which module computes/enforces the per-run spool total limit at write time, and which module maps an overflow to `resource_exhausted` (function) vs `contract_violation` (operation)?
options: `store` enforces byte totals and returns typed overflow; caller maps status
`runs` owns all spool-total checks and `effects` delegates file writes through it
`effects`/`runs` each enforce separately for their own producers
open_points.default_guess: `store` enforces totals atomically and returns overflow metadata; `runs`/`effects` map to their required node statuses.
